market_context.summary: Kenyan e-commerce is mobile-first and fragmented: a Communications Authority of Kenya survey for July 2024 to June 2025 found that 44.8% of online orders were placed in mobile apps, 20.2% through WhatsApp and only 12% on websites, with mobile money used by 65.7% of shoppers. Jumia is the largest marketplace by every traffic estimate retrieved and reports beauty and perfumes as its second product category; the classifieds site Jiji and the marketplace Kilimall follow. Supermarket chains (Naivas, Carrefour, Quickmart) and pharmacy chains (Goodlife, Pharmaplus, MYDAWA) sell online through small sites of their own and, more visibly, through Glovo, whose Nairobi 'Pharmacy & Beauty' section also hosts brand shops for Nivea and L'Oreal. The sector has seen failures (Copia Kenya was ordered into liquidation in September 2026), and Glovo's parent is the subject of a takeover offer from Uber. No official statistic on the size of online beauty sales was found.

key_facts.fact: Communications Authority of Kenya customer satisfaction survey (1 July 2024 - 30 June 2025): mobile apps accounted for 44.8% of online order placements, WhatsApp 20.2% and website portals 12%; domestic online outlets had 47.7% of usage, marketplaces and social-media commerce 18% and cross-border platforms such as Amazon 13.8%; mobile money was used by 65.7% of shoppers and cash on delivery by 13%. Reported via Business Daily; the original CA report was not retrieved.

Jumia group (all eight countries, physical goods): GMV US$224.0 million, 2.7 million quarterly active customers and 6.3 million orders in the third quarter of 2026. Kenya-only GMV and customer numbers are Not publicly disclosed.

Jumia Kenya describes itself as holding 'the largest market share', with more than 300 pick-up stations in about 100 towns, more than 26,000 JForce agents and 1.4 million products listed; its top product categories are phones, beauty and perfumes, home appliances, men's shoes and TVs. Company claims, not independently verified.
key_facts.source_date: n.d. (2025; cites Jumia Group Q3 2025 results)

key_facts.fact: Website traffic, October 2026 (Similarweb 'Total Visits' on free overview pages): jumia.co.ke 3.8M (Kenya rank 24), jiji.co.ke 2M (rank 45), kilimall.co.ke 469.8K (rank 171), carrefour.ke 312.1K, naivas.online 212.8K, mydawa.com 169.2K, goodlife.co.ke 113.5K, quickmart.co.ke 82.8K, pharmaplus.co.ke 61.3K, lintonsbeauty.com 16.5K. Semrush's October 2026 estimates are lower for jumia.co.ke (1.62M) and jiji.co.ke (1.25M).

Glovo holds about 33% of online food delivery and 46% of grocery delivery in Kenya according to the Competition Authority of Kenya's most recent market study, as reported by Techweez (study year not given). Uber announced a takeover offer for Glovo's parent Delivery Hero in July 2026, expected to complete in the second half of 2027 subject to approvals.
Copia Kenya, a rural e-commerce company, was ordered into liquidation by the High Court in September 2026 after two years in administration (court order, reported by Techweez).

Kenya had 23.4 million internet users (40.5% penetration) at the end of 2025; TikTok's adult advertising reach was 18.4 million, Facebook's 17.0 million and Instagram's 3.95 million. No WhatsApp figure is given.

ranking_method_note: weighted_score = 0.20 x ecommerce_significance + 0.25 x beauty_category_relevance + 0.20 x consumer_reach + 0.15 x brand_competitor_coverage + 0.20 x data_integration_feasibility, each scored 1-5, rounded to 2 decimals. priority_rank orders platforms by weighted_score within the country (1 = highest); ties are broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach, as the rubric requires. Where platforms were still tied, ecommerce_significance, then data_integration_feasibility, then name were used (our addition; the rubric stops earlier). Scores are analyst judgements anchored to the evidence note beside each score. Anchors for brand_competitor_coverage (thirteen reference brands): 5 = at least 11 confirmed with real depth, or every brand tested when at least 8 were tested; 4 = 8-10 confirmed, or 11+ confirmed with thin listings; 3 = 4-7 confirmed; 2 = 1-3 confirmed; 1 = none found. Where a catalogue could not be read at all the score is a placeholder marked UNVERIFIED: 3 (neutral) for pharmacies, grocers and general marketplaces that normally stock the category, 2 for delivery apps and classifieds, 1 for cross-border value or fashion platforms and private messaging. competitor_presence.level follows the same evidence: high = score 4-5, medium = 3, low = 1-2, unknown = placeholder. Anchors for data_integration_feasibility: 5 = documented seller API plus openly readable pages, 4 = openly readable pages or feeds, 3 = partly readable or seller-portal access only, 2 = automated access refused, 1 = app-only, login wall or CAPTCHA. Closed platforms therefore rank lower for reasons of access, not commercial weight. For Kenya this mainly affects Naivas, Carrefour, Quickmart and Jiji; the supermarkets are visible through Glovo, which is one reason Glovo ranks second.

competitor_presence.note: Verified on 2026-11-26 from Jumia Kenya public catalogue pages retrieved with the WebFetch tool (a plain HTTP request received a 403 challenge and was not retried). Catalogue searches ('products found'): Colgate 266, Dark and Lovely 138, Pantene 135, Sensodyne 32, Sunsilk 6; a Head & Shoulders search (221 loosely matched results) showed a Head & Shoulders brand filter. The Health & Beauty brand filter lists Dabur, Dove, Himalaya, Cantu and ORS, and product titles or brand-store logos on the category page show Garnier, Nivea, L'Oreal Professionnel, Vaseline and CeraVe. A host named vendor-api.jumia.com answers with an API-gateway message, which suggests a vendor API exists, but no public documentation was found in this session (UNVERIFIED).

platforms.data_collection_feasibility_note: Category and search pages were readable through a standard fetch tool, but direct HTTP requests met a Cloudflare challenge, so large-scale collection is uncertain. Own-listing data is available to registered vendors through Vendor Center. Check Jumia's terms before automated collection.

ecommerce_significance.note: Largest Kenyan e-commerce site by both traffic estimators; claims the largest market share.

beauty_category_relevance.note: Beauty and perfumes is its second product category and 301,425 health and beauty products are listed.

consumer_reach.note: 3.8M visits (Similarweb) and Kenya rank 24, far ahead of other retail sites.

brand_competitor_coverage.note: All thirteen reference brands found (L'Oreal as L'Oreal Professionnel), with depth for Colgate (266), Dark and Lovely (138) and Pantene (135).

data_integration_feasibility.note: Public pages readable but challenge-protected; vendor portal for own data; no documented API found.

platforms.priority_rationale: Clear first priority in Kenya: largest audience, beauty is a top category, widest verified brand coverage, and the brand owner of Dark and Lovely already points shoppers to it.
platforms.confidence_note: Traffic estimates from two providers differ by more than a factor of two and Kenya-level sales are not disclosed; category and brand evidence was verified directly.

platforms.operator: Glovo (owned by Delivery Hero; Uber announced a takeover offer for Delivery Hero in July 2026, completion expected in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory approval)
platforms.beauty_relevance_note: Glovo's Nairobi 'Pharmacy & Beauty' section lists beauty chains and pharmacies (Super Cosmetics, Goodlife Pharmacy and Goodlife Pharmacy Beauty, Pharma Plus and Pharma Plus - Beauty, MYDAWA, Lintons' Beauty Box, True Cosmetics, Yves Rocher, Glovo Beauty World) and brand shops named 'NIVEA Beauty Shop' and 'Loreal Beauty Shop'. Its Groceries section lists Naivas, Carrefour, Quickmart and Chandarana Foodplus.
platforms.pharmacy_relevance_note: Dozens of pharmacies are listed, including the main chains (Goodlife, Pharma Plus, MYDAWA).
platforms.market_importance_note: Estimate: tier 1 for on-demand retail, resting on regulator-study shares reported in the press (33% of food delivery, 46% of grocery delivery) and more than 6,000 merchants.

consumer_reach_evidence.claim: Glovo holds about 33% of online food delivery and 46% of grocery delivery in Kenya, per the Competition Authority of Kenya's most recent market study as reported by Techweez. VERIFIED source type (regulator study), but cited second-hand and the study year is not given.
More than 6,000 merchants, about 2,200 riders daily and operations in 12 towns.
Order growth of 40% year on year and more than KSh20bn of cumulative sales for merchant partners since 2019.
Weekly app downloads of roughly 15,000-17,700 in Kenya; Uber Eats peaked at about 20,800 in early November 2025 and Bolt Food reached about 8,300 (Sensor Tower estimates). Dated: about 12 months old.

competitor_presence.note: Verified on 2026-11-26 from Glovo's public Nairobi pages (plain HTTP requests, no login). The Pharmacy & Beauty listing includes 'NIVEA Beauty Shop' and 'Loreal Beauty Shop'; store pages show Dove, Garnier, Nivea and Vaseline at Naivas, Carrefour and Quickmart, and L'Oreal, Garnier, Nivea, Cantu and CeraVe at Super Cosmetics. Oral-care brands (Colgate, Sensodyne) and Pantene were not seen on the page excerpts read, so they are UNVERIFIED.

platforms.product_coverage_note: Aggregates the assortments of the main supermarket, pharmacy and beauty chains plus brand-run shops; store pages show categories, prices and promotions for the Nairobi delivery area.

api_availability.note: Glovo publishes a 'Glovo Partners API' (OpenAPI definition) for point-of-sale integrators and vendors that sell through Glovo: order webhooks and menu or product updates, with credentials issued on request. It does not give brand owners access to other merchants' data; availability for Kenyan stores is UNVERIFIED.

platforms.data_collection_feasibility_note: Category and store pages for Nairobi were served to plain HTTP requests without login or challenge and list stores, product categories and promotions; full product lists depend on a delivery address. Check Glovo's terms before automated collection.

ecommerce_significance.note: Largest delivery platform by the regulator-study shares reported (33% food, 46% grocery).

beauty_category_relevance.note: Hosts the main beauty and pharmacy chains and brand shops for Nivea and L'Oreal.

consumer_reach.note: 6,000+ merchants in 12 towns; no user count disclosed.

brand_competitor_coverage.note: Five target brands seen across store pages (L'Oreal, Garnier, Nivea, Dove, Vaseline); oral care and Pantene UNVERIFIED.

data_integration_feasibility.note: Store pages are openly readable, though full product lists need a delivery address; the documented API is for vendors only.

platforms.priority_rationale: Second priority and the most efficient single window onto Kenyan modern trade: one platform exposes supermarket, pharmacy and beauty-chain assortments that are otherwise blocked or thin on the retailers' own sites. Reservation: ownership is due to change if Uber's offer completes.
platforms.confidence_note: Market shares come from a regulator study cited second-hand without a year; store and brand evidence was verified directly; user numbers are not disclosed.
